# Weather Data Exploratory Analysis - Hierarchical Structure

# I. Data Import and Pre-processing

## I.1. Initial Data Loading and Column Standardization

**Description:** Load the raw weather dataset with proper encoding handling (Latin-1), standardize column names by removing special characters and French accents, and convert data types appropriately. This establishes a clean foundation for all subsequent analyses.

```{r}
# Load necessary packages
library(pacman)
p_load(
  dplyr, readr, lubridate, tidyr, stringr, skimr,
  VIM, summarytools, corrplot, janitor, purrr
)

# Set working directory (adjust path as needed)
setwd("C:/Users/U078-N800/Desktop/Ml_Internship/Copy")

# Load the weather dataset with Latin-1 encoding
weather_data <- read.csv("BD_weather.csv", 
                        sep = ";", 
                        dec = ",", 
                        header = TRUE, 
                        stringsAsFactors = FALSE, 
                        fileEncoding = "latin1")

# Display original column names
cat("Original column names:\n")
print(colnames(weather_data))

# Clean and rename columns for better readability and coding
weather_data <- weather_data %>%
  rename(
    # Basic temperature variables
    date = Date,
    temp_min = T..C..mini,
    temp_max = T..C..maxi,
    temp_mean = T..C..moy,
    temp_amplitude = Ampl,
    
    # Evaporation variables
    evap_c2 = Ev..C2.,
    evap_km8 = Ev..Km8.,
    evap_mean = Ev..moy.,
    evap_bardial = Ev..Bardial.,
    
    # Solar and cloud variables
    insolation = Insolation,
    radiation = Radiation,
    cloud_6h = Neb..6.h,
    cloud_16h = Neb..16.h,
    
    # Humidity variables
    humidity_min = H.Mini,
    humidity_max = H.Maxi,
    humidity_mean = H.Moy,
    humidity_6h = H.6.h,
    humidity_12h = H.12.h,
    humidity_16h = H.16.h,
    humidity_24h = H.24.h,
    
    # IGN measurements
    ign_senegal = IGN.Sénégal,
    ign_guiers = IGN.Guiers,
    ign_guiers_x6 = IGN.Guiers.X6,
    temp_senegal = T..C..Sénégal,
    temp_canal_a = T..C..Canal.A,
    
    # Soil temperature measurements (N = Natural?)
    temp_6h_10cm_n = T.6h.10.cm.N,
    temp_16h_10cm_n = T.16h.10.cm.N,
    temp_6h_20cm_n = T.6h.20.cm.N,
    temp_16h_20cm_n = T.16h.20.cm.N,
    temp_6h_30cm_n = T.6h.30.cm.N,
    temp_16h_30cm_n = T.16h.30.cm.N,
    temp_6h_50cm_n = T.6h.50.cm.N,
    temp_16h_50cm_n = T.16h.50.cm.N,
    
    # Soil temperature measurements (Ir = Irrigated?)
    temp_6h_10cm_ir = T.6h.10.cm.Ir,
    temp_16h_10cm_ir = T.16h.10.cm.Ir,
    temp_6h_20cm_ir = T.6h.20.cm.Ir,
    temp_16h_20cm_ir = T.16h.20.cm.Ir,
    temp_6h_30cm_ir = T.6h.30.cm.Ir,
    temp_16h_30cm_ir = T.16h.30.cm.Ir,
    temp_6h_50cm_ir = T.6h.50.cm.Ir,
    temp_16h_50cm_ir = T.16h.50.cm.Ir,
    
    # Soil temperature measurements (In = ?)
    temp_6h_10cm_in = T.6h.10.cm.In,
    temp_16h_10cm_in = T.16h.10.cm.In,
    temp_6h_20cm_in = T.6h.20.cm.In,
    temp_16h_20cm_in = T.16h.20.cm.In,
    
    # Date and time variables
    year = Année,
    month = Mois,
    day = Jour,
    decade_1 = Décade.1,
    decade = Décade,
    date_2 = Date.2,
    week = Semaine,
    day_of_year = A.ce.jour,
    
    # Key variables
    key_0 = Clé.0,
    key_01 = Clé.01,
    key_1 = Clé.1,
    key_2 = Clé2,
    period = Période
  )

# Convert data types appropriately
weather_data <- weather_data %>%
  mutate(
    # Convert date column
    date = dmy(date),
    
    # Convert numeric columns (all temperature, humidity, evaporation, etc.)
    across(c(temp_min, temp_max, temp_mean, temp_amplitude,
             evap_c2, evap_km8, evap_mean, evap_bardial,
             insolation, radiation, cloud_6h, cloud_16h,
             humidity_min, humidity_max, humidity_mean, 
             humidity_6h, humidity_12h, humidity_16h, humidity_24h,
             ign_senegal, ign_guiers, ign_guiers_x6,
             temp_senegal, temp_canal_a,
             starts_with("temp_")), 
           ~ as.numeric(gsub(",", ".", as.character(.)))),
    
    # Convert key variables to factors
    across(c(key_0, key_01, key_1, key_2), as.factor),
    
    # Convert other categorical variables to factors
    period = as.factor(period),
    month = as.factor(month),
    
    # Keep numeric for time-related variables
    year = as.numeric(year),
    day = as.numeric(day),
    decade_1 = as.numeric(decade_1),
    decade = as.numeric(decade),
    date_2 = as.numeric(date_2),
    week = as.numeric(week),
    day_of_year = as.numeric(day_of_year)
  )

# Display cleaned column names
cat("\nCleaned column names:\n")
print(colnames(weather_data))

# Display basic information about the dataset
cat("\nDataset dimensions:", dim(weather_data), "\n")
cat("Number of rows:", nrow(weather_data), "\n")

str(weather_data)

# Check data types
cat("\nData types after conversion:\n")

data_types_df <- data.frame(
  column = names(data_types),
  type = as.character(data_types)
) %>%
  arrange(type, column)
print(data_types_df)

# Check for missing values
cat("\nMissing values summary:\n")
missing_summary <- weather_data %>%
  summarise_all(~sum(is.na(.))) %>%
  gather(column, missing_count) %>%
  arrange(desc(missing_count))
print(missing_summary)

# Summary statistics for main temperature variables
cat("\nSummary statistics for main temperature variables:\n")
temp_main_vars <- c("temp_min", "temp_max", "temp_mean", "temp_amplitude")
print(summary(weather_data[, temp_main_vars]))

# Summary statistics for humidity variables

# Summary statistics for evaporation variables

evap_vars <- c("evap_c2", "evap_km8", "evap_mean", "evap_bardial")
print(summary(weather_data[, evap_vars]))

# Check factor levels for key variables
cat("\nFactor levels for key variables:\n")
factor_vars <- c("key_0", "key_01", "key_1", "key_2", "period", "month")
for(var in factor_vars) {

# Date range information

sapply(weather_data, class) %>%

}
```

# II. Data Quality Assessment

## II.1. Missing Values Analysis

**Description:** Comprehensive examination of data completeness across all variables using multiple visualization techniques. Calculate missing value percentages, identify patterns in data gaps, and assess temporal coverage for each weather variable.

```{r}
# Load necessary packages
library(pacman)
p_load(
  dplyr, readr, lubridate, tidyr, stringr, ggplot2,
  knitr, kableExtra, VIM, viridis, forcats
)

# Comprehensive missing data assessment for weather data with NA handling
comprehensive_weather_analysis <- function(data, weather_vars) {
  
  # Function to safely calculate statistics for variables with all NA values
  safe_calc <- function(x, func) {
    values <- data[[x]][!is.na(data[[x]])]
    if(length(values) == 0) {
      return(NA)
    } else {
      return(func(values))
    }
  }
  
  # Basic missing data statistics
  missing_stats <- data.frame(
    Variable = weather_vars,
    Total_Records = nrow(data),
    Valid_Records = sapply(weather_vars, function(x) sum(!is.na(data[[x]]))),
    Missing_Records = sapply(weather_vars, function(x) sum(is.na(data[[x]]))),
    Zero_Records = sapply(weather_vars, function(x) sum(data[[x]] == 0, na.rm = TRUE)),
    Valid_Percentage = sapply(weather_vars, function(x) 
      round(100 * sum(!is.na(data[[x]])) / nrow(data), 2)),
    Missing_Percentage = sapply(weather_vars, function(x) 
      round(100 * sum(is.na(data[[x]])) / nrow(data), 2)),
    First_Record = sapply(weather_vars, function(x) {
      valid_dates <- data$date[!is.na(data[[x]])]
      if(length(valid_dates) > 0) min(valid_dates) else NA
    }),
    Last_Record = sapply(weather_vars, function(x) {
      valid_dates <- data$date[!is.na(data[[x]])]
      if(length(valid_dates) > 0) max(valid_dates) else NA
    }),
    Mean_Value = sapply(weather_vars, function(x) {
      val <- safe_calc(x, mean)
      if(is.na(val)) NA else round(val, 2)
    }),
    Median_Value = sapply(weather_vars, function(x) {
      val <- safe_calc(x, median)
      if(is.na(val)) NA else round(val, 2)
    }),
    Max_Value = sapply(weather_vars, function(x) {
      val <- safe_calc(x, max)
      if(is.na(val)) NA else round(val, 2)
    }),
    Min_Value = sapply(weather_vars, function(x) {
      val <- safe_calc(x, min)
      if(is.na(val)) NA else round(val, 2)
    }),
    SD_Value = sapply(weather_vars, function(x) {
      val <- safe_calc(x, sd)
      if(is.na(val)) NA else round(val, 2)
    }),
    CV_Value = sapply(weather_vars, function(x) {
      values <- data[[x]][!is.na(data[[x]])]
      if(length(values) == 0) {
        return(NA)
      }
      mean_val <- mean(values)
      sd_val <- sd(values)
      if(is.na(mean_val) || is.na(sd_val) || mean_val <= 0) {
        return(NA)
      } else {
        return(round(sd_val/mean_val, 3))
      }
    })
  )
  
  # Calculate operational periods (handle NA dates)
  missing_stats$Operational_Days <- ifelse(
    is.na(missing_stats$First_Record) | is.na(missing_stats$Last_Record),
    NA,
    as.numeric(missing_stats$Last_Record - missing_stats$First_Record) + 1
  )
  
  missing_stats$Data_Density <- ifelse(
    is.na(missing_stats$Operational_Days) | missing_stats$Operational_Days == 0,
    NA,
    round(missing_stats$Valid_Records / missing_stats$Operational_Days, 3)
  )
  
  return(missing_stats)
}

# Monthly observation counts for each variable
create_monthly_summary <- function(data, weather_vars) {
  
  # Create monthly summary for all variables
  monthly_summary <- data %>%
    select(date, all_of(weather_vars)) %>%
    mutate(
      Year = year(date),
      Month = month(date),
      YearMonth = paste0(Year, "-", sprintf("%02d", Month))
    ) %>%
    group_by(Year, Month, YearMonth) %>%
    summarise(
      across(all_of(weather_vars), list(
        valid_obs = ~ sum(!is.na(.)),
        total_days = ~ n(),
        missing_obs = ~ sum(is.na(.)),
        completeness_pct = ~ round(100 * sum(!is.na(.)) / n(), 1)
      ), .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"),
      days_in_month = n(),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  return(monthly_summary)
}

# Get all numeric variables from the dataset (excluding date and factor variables)

  select_if(function(x) is.numeric(x) && sum(!is.na(x)) > 0) %>%
  names()

all_weather_vars <- setdiff(all_numeric_vars, exclude_vars)

print(excluded_vars)

# Run comprehensive analysis on ALL variables
weather_comprehensive <- comprehensive_weather_analysis(weather_data, all_weather_vars)

# Create monthly summary for ALL variables

# Save detailed summaries to CSV
write.csv(weather_comprehensive, "weather_all_variables_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(monthly_weather_summary, "weather_all_monthly_observations.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Create and display formatted summary table for ALL variables
formatted_summary <- weather_comprehensive %>%

# Enhanced missing data visualization for weather data
create_weather_visualizations <- function(data, weather_vars) {
  
  # 1. Missing data pattern heatmap by variable and month
  missing_pattern <- data %>%
    select(date, all_of(weather_vars)) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = -date, names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Value") %>%
    mutate(
      Data_Status = case_when(
        is.na(Value) ~ "Missing",
        Value == 0 ~ "Zero",
        TRUE ~ "Available"
      ),
      Year = year(date),
      Month = month(date),
      YearMonth = paste0(Year, "-", sprintf("%02d", Month))
    ) %>%
    group_by(Variable, Year, Month, YearMonth) %>%
    summarise(
      Missing_Days = sum(is.na(Value)),
      Total_Days = n(),
      Missing_Pct = Missing_Days / Total_Days,
      Status = case_when(
        Missing_Pct >= 0.5 ~ "Missing",
        Missing_Pct >= 0.1 ~ "Partial",
        TRUE ~ "Complete"
      ),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  # Create heatmap
  p1 <- ggplot(missing_pattern, aes(x = factor(Month), y = Variable)) +
    geom_tile(aes(fill = Status), color = "white", size = 0.3) +
    facet_wrap(~Year, ncol = 4, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c("Missing" = "#d73027",    # Red for missing
                "Partial" = "#fdae61",     # Orange for partial
                "Complete" = "#4575b4"),   # Blue for complete
      name = "Data\nStatus"
    ) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = month.abb) +
    labs(title = "Weather Data Availability Heatmap by Variable and Year",
         subtitle = "Monthly data completeness for each weather variable",
         x = "Month", y = "Weather Variable") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 9),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
      strip.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "right",
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11)
    )
  
  # 2. Data completeness over time
  completeness_over_time <- data %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(
      Available_Variables = sum(!is.na(c_across(all_of(weather_vars)))),
      Percentage_Available = 100 * Available_Variables / length(weather_vars)
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  p2 <- ggplot(completeness_over_time, aes(x = date, y = Percentage_Available)) +
    geom_line(color = "steelblue", size = 0.5) +
    geom_smooth(method = "loess", color = "red", se = TRUE) +
    labs(title = "Weather Data Completeness Over Time",
         x = "Date", y = "Percentage of Variables Available (%)") +
    theme_minimal()
  
  # 3. Variable operational periods
  operational_periods <- weather_comprehensive %>%
    select(Variable, First_Record, Last_Record, Valid_Percentage) %>%
    mutate(
      Variable = fct_reorder(Variable, as.numeric(First_Record)),
      Duration_Days = as.numeric(Last_Record - First_Record) + 1
    )
  
  p3 <- ggplot(operational_periods) +
    geom_segment(aes(x = First_Record, xend = Last_Record, 
                    y = Variable, yend = Variable, 
                    color = Valid_Percentage), size = 3) +
    geom_point(aes(x = First_Record, y = Variable), color = "darkgreen", size = 2) +
    geom_point(aes(x = Last_Record, y = Variable), color = "darkred", size = 2) +
    scale_color_viridis_c(name = "Data\nCompleteness\n(%)") +
    labs(title = "Weather Variable Operational Periods",
         subtitle = "Green dots = start date, Red dots = end date",
         x = "Date", y = "Weather Variable") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9)
    )
  
  # 4. Monthly observation counts heatmap
  monthly_obs_long <- monthly_weather_summary %>%
    select(Year, Month, YearMonth, ends_with("_valid_obs")) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = ends_with("_valid_obs"), 
                names_to = "Variable", 
                values_to = "Valid_Obs") %>%
    mutate(Variable = gsub("_valid_obs", "", Variable))
  
  p4 <- ggplot(monthly_obs_long, aes(x = factor(Month), y = Variable, fill = Valid_Obs)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", size = 0.3) +
    facet_wrap(~Year, ncol = 4) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Valid\nObservations") +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = month.abb) +
    labs(title = "Monthly Observation Counts by Variable",
         subtitle = "Number of valid daily observations per month",
         x = "Month", y = "Weather Variable") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 9),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
      strip.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "right",
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold")
    )
  
  return(list(
    pattern_heatmap = p1, 
    completeness_trend = p2, 
    operational_periods = p3,
    monthly_counts = p4
  ))
}

}

# Show variables with perfect data (100%)
perfect_vars <- weather_comprehensive$Variable[weather_comprehensive$Valid_Percentage == 100]
if(length(perfect_vars) > 0) {
  cat("\nVariables with 100% complete data:\n")
  cat(paste(perfect_vars, collapse = ", "), "\n")
}

# Show variables with significant missing data (>20% missing but not 100%)
missing_vars <- weather_comprehensive$Variable[weather_comprehensive$Missing_Percentage > 20 & weather_comprehensive$Missing_Percentage < 100]
if(length(missing_vars) > 0) {
  cat("\nVariables with >20% missing data (but not completely empty):\n")
  missing_details <- weather_comprehensive[weather_comprehensive$Variable %in% missing_vars, 
                                         c("Variable", "Missing_Percentage", "Valid_Records")]
  print(missing_details)
}
```

## II.2. Temporal Data Availability Assessment

**Description:** Analyze when and how consistently data was collected for each variable. Identify operational periods, seasonal patterns, and systematic gaps that may affect modeling decisions.

```{r}
# Monthly observation counts and summary for each variable
create_monthly_summary <- function(data, weather_vars) {
  
  # Create monthly summary for all variables
  monthly_summary <- data %>%
    select(date, all_of(weather_vars)) %>%
    mutate(
      Year = year(date),
      Month = month(date),
      Month_Name = month.name[Month],
      YearMonth = paste0(Year, "-", sprintf("%02d", Month)),
      Days_In_Month = days_in_month(date)
    ) %>%
    group_by(Year, Month, Month_Name, YearMonth, Days_In_Month) %>%
    summarise(
      month_start = min(date),
      month_end = max(date),
      actual_days_in_data = n(),
      across(all_of(weather_vars), list(
        valid_obs = ~ sum(!is.na(.)),
        missing_obs = ~ sum(is.na(.)),
        completeness_pct = ~ round(100 * sum(!is.na(.)) / n(), 1),
        zero_obs = ~ sum(. == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
      ), .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    arrange(Year, Month)
  
  return(monthly_summary)
}

# Create comprehensive monthly analysis by variable
create_monthly_variable_analysis <- function(monthly_data, weather_vars) {
  
  # Extract valid observations for each variable
  valid_obs_cols <- paste0(weather_vars, "_valid_obs")
  completeness_cols <- paste0(weather_vars, "_completeness_pct")
  
  monthly_analysis <- monthly_data %>%
    select(Year, Month, Month_Name, YearMonth, Days_In_Month, actual_days_in_data, 
           all_of(valid_obs_cols), all_of(completeness_cols)) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = all_of(valid_obs_cols),
      names_to = "Variable", 
      values_to = "Valid_Days"
    ) %>%
    mutate(Variable = gsub("_valid_obs", "", Variable)) %>%
    # Add completeness percentage
    left_join(
      monthly_data %>%
        select(Year, Month, YearMonth, all_of(completeness_cols)) %>%
        pivot_longer(
          cols = all_of(completeness_cols),
          names_to = "Variable_Comp",
          values_to = "Completeness_Pct"
        ) %>%
        mutate(Variable = gsub("_completeness_pct", "", Variable_Comp)) %>%
        select(Year, Month, YearMonth, Variable, Completeness_Pct),
      by = c("Year", "Month", "YearMonth", "Variable")
    ) %>%
    group_by(Variable, Year) %>%
    summarise(
      Total_Months = n(),
      Total_Possible_Days = sum(Days_In_Month),
      Total_Actual_Days = sum(actual_days_in_data),
      Total_Valid_Days = sum(Valid_Days),
      Total_Missing_Days = Total_Actual_Days - Total_Valid_Days,
      
      # Monthly completeness statistics
      Months_Complete = sum(Completeness_Pct == 100),
      Months_Near_Complete = sum(Completeness_Pct >= 90 & Completeness_Pct < 100),
      Months_Partial = sum(Completeness_Pct > 10 & Completeness_Pct < 90),
      Months_Poor = sum(Completeness_Pct > 0 & Completeness_Pct <= 10),
      Months_Empty = sum(Completeness_Pct == 0),
      
      # Percentages
      Month_Complete_Pct = round(100 * Months_Complete / Total_Months, 1),
      Month_Near_Complete_Pct = round(100 * Months_Near_Complete / Total_Months, 1),
      Month_Partial_Pct = round(100 * Months_Partial / Total_Months, 1),
      Month_Poor_Pct = round(100 * Months_Poor / Total_Months, 1),
      Month_Empty_Pct = round(100 * Months_Empty / Total_Months, 1),
      
      # Overall data density
      Overall_Completeness_Pct = round(100 * Total_Valid_Days / Total_Actual_Days, 1),
      
      # Monthly statistics
      Min_Days_Per_Month = min(Valid_Days),
      Max_Days_Per_Month = max(Valid_Days),
      Mean_Days_Per_Month = round(mean(Valid_Days), 1),
      Median_Days_Per_Month = round(median(Valid_Days), 1),
      
      # Seasonal analysis
      Spring_Months = sum(Month %in% c(3,4,5)),
      Summer_Months = sum(Month %in% c(6,7,8)),
      Fall_Months = sum(Month %in% c(9,10,11)),
      Winter_Months = sum(Month %in% c(12,1,2)),
      
      Spring_Valid_Days = sum(Valid_Days[Month %in% c(3,4,5)]),
      Summer_Valid_Days = sum(Valid_Days[Month %in% c(6,7,8)]),
      Fall_Valid_Days = sum(Valid_Days[Month %in% c(9,10,11)]),
      Winter_Valid_Days = sum(Valid_Days[Month %in% c(12,1,2)]),
      
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    arrange(Variable, Year)
  
  return(monthly_analysis)
}

# Create annual summary by variable
create_annual_variable_summary <- function(monthly_analysis) {
  
  annual_summary <- monthly_analysis %>%
    group_by(Variable) %>%
    summarise(
      Years_Available = n(),
      First_Year = min(Year),
      Last_Year = max(Year),
      
      # Totals across all years
      Total_Months_All_Years = sum(Total_Months),
      Total_Days_All_Years = sum(Total_Actual_Days),
      Total_Valid_Days_All_Years = sum(Total_Valid_Days),
      
      # Average statistics across years
      Avg_Months_Complete = round(mean(Months_Complete), 1),
      Avg_Months_Near_Complete = round(mean(Months_Near_Complete), 1),
      Avg_Months_Partial = round(mean(Months_Partial), 1),
      Avg_Months_Poor = round(mean(Months_Poor), 1),
      Avg_Months_Empty = round(mean(Months_Empty), 1),
      
      # Overall percentages across all years
      Overall_Month_Complete = round(100 * sum(Months_Complete) / sum(Total_Months), 1),
      Overall_Month_Near_Complete = round(100 * sum(Months_Near_Complete) / sum(Total_Months), 1),
      Overall_Month_Partial = round(100 * sum(Months_Partial) / sum(Total_Months), 1),
      Overall_Month_Poor = round(100 * sum(Months_Poor) / sum(Total_Months), 1),
      Overall_Month_Empty = round(100 * sum(Months_Empty) / sum(Total_Months), 1),
      Overall_Data_Completeness = round(100 * sum(Total_Valid_Days) / sum(Total_Actual_Days), 1),
      
      # Seasonal analysis
      Spring_Completeness = round(100 * sum(Spring_Valid_Days) / sum(Spring_Months * 31), 1),  # Approximate
      Summer_Completeness = round(100 * sum(Summer_Valid_Days) / sum(Summer_Months * 31), 1),
      Fall_Completeness = round(100 * sum(Fall_Valid_Days) / sum(Fall_Months * 30), 1),
      Winter_Completeness = round(100 * sum(Winter_Valid_Days) / sum(Winter_Months * 31), 1),
      
      # Daily statistics
      Overall_Avg_Days_Per_Month = round(mean(Mean_Days_Per_Month), 1),
      Overall_Min_Days_Per_Month = min(Min_Days_Per_Month),
      Overall_Max_Days_Per_Month = max(Max_Days_Per_Month),
      
      # Quality rating
      Quality_Rating = case_when(
        Overall_Data_Completeness >= 95 ~ "Excellent",
        Overall_Data_Completeness >= 80 ~ "Good",
        Overall_Data_Completeness >= 60 ~ "Fair",
        TRUE ~ "Poor"
      ),
      
      # Data consistency rating
      Consistency_Rating = case_when(
        Overall_Month_Complete >= 80 ~ "Very Consistent",
        Overall_Month_Complete + Overall_Month_Near_Complete >= 80 ~ "Consistent",
        Overall_Month_Empty < 20 ~ "Moderate",
        TRUE ~ "Inconsistent"
      ),
      
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    arrange(desc(Overall_Data_Completeness))
  
  return(annual_summary)
}

# Create month-by-month heatmap data
create_monthly_heatmap_data <- function(monthly_data, weather_vars) {
  
  valid_obs_cols <- paste0(weather_vars, "_valid_obs")
  
  heatmap_data <- monthly_data %>%
    select(Year, Month, Month_Name, all_of(valid_obs_cols)) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = all_of(valid_obs_cols),
      names_to = "Variable",
      values_to = "Valid_Days"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      Variable = gsub("_valid_obs", "", Variable),
      Data_Quality = case_when(
        Valid_Days >= 28 ~ "Complete",
        Valid_Days >= 20 ~ "Good",
        Valid_Days >= 10 ~ "Partial",
        Valid_Days > 0 ~ "Poor",
        TRUE ~ "Empty"
      )
    )
  
  return(heatmap_data)
}
```

## II.3. Monthly Weather Data Availability + Plots

```{r}
# Monthly Weather Data Availability Analysis - Comprehensive Version
# Required libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(lubridate)
library(viridis)
library(RColorBrewer)

# Function to create monthly data summary with proper NA handling
create_monthly_weather_summary <- function(data, weather_vars) {
  
  # Create monthly summary for each weather variable
  monthly_summary <- data %>%
    select(date, all_of(weather_vars)) %>%
    mutate(
      Year = year(date),
      Month = month(date),
      Month_Name = month.abb[Month]
    ) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = -c(date, Year, Month, Month_Name), 
                 names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Value") %>%
    group_by(Variable, Year, Month, Month_Name) %>%
    summarise(
      Total_Days_In_Dataset = n(),
      Valid_Days = sum(!is.na(Value)),
      Missing_Days = sum(is.na(Value)),
      Zero_Days = sum(Value == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
      # Calculate actual days in month for proper completeness calculation
      Days_In_Month = days_in_month(as.Date(paste(Year, Month, "01", sep = "-"))),
      # Fix: Set completeness based on valid days / actual days in month
      Completeness_Pct = ifelse(Valid_Days == 0, NA, round(100 * Valid_Days / Days_In_Month, 1)),
      # Fix: Set weather statistics to NA when no valid data exists
      Mean_Daily_Value = ifelse(Valid_Days == 0, NA, round(mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE), 2)),
      Max_Daily_Value = ifelse(Valid_Days == 0, NA, round(max(Value, na.rm = TRUE), 2)),
      Min_Daily_Value = ifelse(Valid_Days == 0, NA, round(min(Value, na.rm = TRUE), 2)),
      SD_Daily_Value = ifelse(Valid_Days == 0, NA, round(sd(Value, na.rm = TRUE), 2)),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    arrange(Variable, Year, Month)
  
  return(monthly_summary)
}

# Create the monthly summary using the weather variables from your analysis
cat("Creating monthly weather data summary...\n")
monthly_weather_data <- create_monthly_weather_summary(weather_data, all_weather_vars)

# Display first few rows
cat("=== Monthly Weather Data Summary (First 20 rows) ===\n")
print(head(monthly_weather_data, 20))

# Save detailed summary to CSV
write.csv(monthly_weather_data, "monthly_weather_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nDetailed monthly summary saved to: monthly_weather_summary.csv\n")

# Create summary statistics by variable - handle NA values properly
variable_monthly_stats <- monthly_weather_data %>%
  group_by(Variable) %>%
  summarise(
    Total_Months = n(),
    # Count months with actual data (not NA)
    Months_With_Data = sum(!is.na(Completeness_Pct)),
    Complete_Months = sum(Completeness_Pct == 100, na.rm = TRUE),
    Near_Complete_Months = sum(Completeness_Pct >= 90 & Completeness_Pct < 100, na.rm = TRUE),
    Partial_Months = sum(Completeness_Pct > 10 & Completeness_Pct < 90, na.rm = TRUE),
    Poor_Months = sum(Completeness_Pct > 0 & Completeness_Pct <= 10, na.rm = TRUE),
    Missing_Months = sum(is.na(Completeness_Pct) | Completeness_Pct == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    # Calculate averages only for months with data
    Avg_Monthly_Completeness = ifelse(Months_With_Data == 0, NA, 
                                    round(mean(Completeness_Pct, na.rm = TRUE), 1)),
    Min_Monthly_Completeness = ifelse(Months_With_Data == 0, NA, 
                                    min(Completeness_Pct, na.rm = TRUE)),
    Max_Monthly_Completeness = ifelse(Months_With_Data == 0, NA, 
                                    max(Completeness_Pct, na.rm = TRUE)),
    Total_Valid_Days = sum(Valid_Days, na.rm = TRUE),
    # Data quality rating
    Quality_Rating = case_when(
      is.na(Avg_Monthly_Completeness) ~ "No Data",
      Avg_Monthly_Completeness >= 95 ~ "Excellent",
      Avg_Monthly_Completeness >= 80 ~ "Good", 
      Avg_Monthly_Completeness >= 60 ~ "Fair",
      TRUE ~ "Poor"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Avg_Monthly_Completeness))

cat("\n=== Variable Monthly Statistics Summary ===\n")
print(head(variable_monthly_stats, 25))

# Save variable summary
write.csv(variable_monthly_stats, "variable_monthly_stats.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Create visualization functions with proper NA handling
create_weather_monthly_visualizations <- function(monthly_data, max_vars_to_show = 50) {
  
  # Filter to top variables for better visualization
  top_variables <- variable_monthly_stats %>%
    head(max_vars_to_show) %>%
    pull(Variable)
  
  monthly_data_filtered <- monthly_data %>%
    filter(Variable %in% top_variables)
  
  # 1. Data Completeness Heatmap - NA values will appear as white/blank
  p1 <- ggplot(monthly_data_filtered, aes(x = Month_Name, y = Variable, fill = Completeness_Pct)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", size = 0.1) +
    facet_wrap(~Year, ncol = 4) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Data\nCompleteness\n(%)", 
                         option = "plasma", direction = 1,
                         na.value = "white") +  # NA values show as white
    scale_x_discrete(limits = month.abb) +
    labs(title = "Monthly Data Completeness by Weather Variable and Year",
         subtitle = paste("Top", max_vars_to_show, "variables by completeness (white = no data)"),
         x = "Month", y = "Weather Variable") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6),
      strip.text = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "right",
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold")
    )
  
  # 2. Number of Valid Days Heatmap
  monthly_data_for_valid_days <- monthly_data_filtered %>%
    mutate(Valid_Days_Display = ifelse(Valid_Days == 0, NA, Valid_Days))
  
  p2 <- ggplot(monthly_data_for_valid_days, aes(x = Month_Name, y = Variable, fill = Valid_Days_Display)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", size = 0.1) +
    facet_wrap(~Year, ncol = 4) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Valid\nDays", option = "viridis",
                         na.value = "white") +
    scale_x_discrete(limits = month.abb) +
    labs(title = "Number of Valid Days per Month by Weather Variable and Year",
         subtitle = paste("Top", max_vars_to_show, "variables (white = no data)"),
         x = "Month", y = "Weather Variable") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6),
      strip.text = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "right",
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold")
    )
  
  # 3. Data Quality Categories Heatmap
  quality_data <- monthly_data_filtered %>%
    mutate(Quality_Category = case_when(
      is.na(Completeness_Pct) | Completeness_Pct == 0 ~ "No Data",
      Completeness_Pct == 100 ~ "Complete",
      Completeness_Pct >= 90 ~ "Near Complete",
      Completeness_Pct >= 70 ~ "Good",
      Completeness_Pct >= 50 ~ "Fair", 
      Completeness_Pct > 0 ~ "Poor",
      TRUE ~ "No Data"
    )) %>%
    mutate(Quality_Category = factor(Quality_Category, 
                                   levels = c("Complete", "Near Complete", "Good", "Fair", "Poor", "No Data")))
  
  p3 <- ggplot(quality_data, aes(x = Month_Name, y = Variable, fill = Quality_Category)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", size = 0.1) +
    facet_wrap(~Year, ncol = 4) +
    scale_fill_manual(name = "Data\nQuality", 
                      values = c("Complete" = "#2166ac", "Near Complete" = "#4393c3", 
                               "Good" = "#92c5de", "Fair" = "#f4a582", 
                               "Poor" = "#d6604d", "No Data" = "white"),
                      drop = FALSE) +
    scale_x_discrete(limits = month.abb) +
    labs(title = "Monthly Data Quality Categories by Weather Variable and Year",
         subtitle = paste("Top", max_vars_to_show, "variables categorized by completeness"),
         x = "Month", y = "Weather Variable") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6),
      strip.text = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "right",
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold")
    )
  
  # 4. Data Availability Timeline
  completeness_timeline <- monthly_data %>%
    mutate(Date_Month = as.Date(paste(Year, Month, "01", sep = "-"))) %>%
    group_by(Date_Month) %>%
    summarise(
      Variables_With_Data = sum(!is.na(Completeness_Pct)),
      Avg_Completeness = ifelse(Variables_With_Data == 0, NA, 
                               mean(Completeness_Pct, na.rm = TRUE)),
      Min_Completeness = ifelse(Variables_With_Data == 0, NA, 
                               min(Completeness_Pct, na.rm = TRUE)),
      Max_Completeness = ifelse(Variables_With_Data == 0, NA, 
                               max(Completeness_Pct, na.rm = TRUE)),
      Variables_Complete = sum(Completeness_Pct == 100, na.rm = TRUE),
      Total_Variables = n(),
      Pct_Variables_Complete = ifelse(Variables_With_Data == 0, 0,
                                    100 * Variables_Complete / Variables_With_Data),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  p4 <- ggplot(completeness_timeline, aes(x = Date_Month)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Min_Completeness, ymax = Max_Completeness), 
                alpha = 0.3, fill = "steelblue", na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_line(aes(y = Avg_Completeness), color = "darkblue", size = 1, na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_line(aes(y = Pct_Variables_Complete), 
              color = "red", size = 1, linetype = "dashed", na.rm = TRUE) +
    labs(title = "Weather Data Completeness Over Time",
         subtitle = "Blue: Average completeness | Red dashed: % variables with complete data | Ribbon: Min-Max range",
         x = "Date", y = "Completeness (%)") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"))
  
  # 5. Variable Performance Overview
  variable_performance <- monthly_data %>%
    group_by(Variable) %>%
    summarise(
      Months_Available = n(),
      Months_With_Data = sum(!is.na(Completeness_Pct)),
      Avg_Completeness = mean(Completeness_Pct, na.rm = TRUE),
      Total_Valid_Days = sum(Valid_Days, na.rm = TRUE),
      Total_Possible_Days = sum(Days_In_Month, na.rm = TRUE),
      Overall_Completeness = ifelse(Total_Possible_Days == 0, 0,
                                   100 * Total_Valid_Days / Total_Possible_Days),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    filter(Months_With_Data > 0) %>%
    arrange(desc(Overall_Completeness)) %>%
    head(30) %>%  # Show top 30 variables
    mutate(Variable = reorder(Variable, Overall_Completeness))
  
  p5 <- ggplot(variable_performance, aes(x = Variable, y = Overall_Completeness)) +
    geom_col(aes(fill = Overall_Completeness), width = 0.8) +
    geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(Overall_Completeness, 1), "%")), 
              hjust = -0.1, size = 2.5) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Completeness\n(%)", option = "plasma") +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(title = "Overall Data Completeness by Weather Variable (Top 30)",
         subtitle = "Based on all available monthly data",
         x = "Weather Variable", y = "Data Completeness (%)") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
      legend.position = "none"
    )
  
  # 6. Seasonal Completeness Patterns
  seasonal_data <- monthly_data %>%
    mutate(Season = case_when(
      Month %in% c(6, 7, 8, 9) ~ "Rainy Season",   # Jun-Sep
      Month %in% c(10, 11, 12, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5) ~ "Dry Season"  # Oct-May
      )) %>%
    group_by(Variable, Season) %>%
    summarise(
      Avg_Completeness = mean(Completeness_Pct, na.rm = TRUE),
      Months_With_Data = sum(!is.na(Completeness_Pct)),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    filter(Months_With_Data > 0) %>%
    # Get top variables for better visualization
    filter(Variable %in% head(variable_monthly_stats$Variable, 30))
  
  p6 <- ggplot(seasonal_data, aes(x = Season, y = Variable, fill = Avg_Completeness)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", size = 0.2) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Avg\nCompleteness\n(%)", option = "mako", na.value = "white") +
    labs(title = "Seasonal Data Completeness Patterns (Top 30 Variables)",
         subtitle = "Average completeness by season across all years",
         x = "Season", y = "Weather Variable") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
      panel.grid = element_blank()
    )
  
  return(list(
    completeness_heatmap = p1,
    valid_days_heatmap = p2,
    quality_categories = p3,
    timeline = p4,
    variable_performance = p5,
    seasonal_patterns = p6
  ))
}
```

```{r}
# Enhanced publication-ready theme with narrow boxplots and clear black contours
publication_theme <- theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    text = element_text(size = 12, family = "Arial", color = "#1C1C1C"),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, color = "#000000", margin = margin(b = 10)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5, color = "#333333", margin = margin(b = 15)),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", color = "#000000", margin = margin(t = 10)),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", color = "#000000", margin = margin(r = 10)),

    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),

    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "#000000", size = 1),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "#000000", size = 1.5),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", color = "#000000"),

    panel.spacing = unit(0.8, "lines"),
    axis.line = element_line(color = "#000000", size = 0.8)
  )

# Function to detect outliers using IQR method
detect_outliers <- function(x) {
  q1 <- quantile(x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
  q3 <- quantile(x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
  iqr <- q3 - q1
  lower_bound <- q1 - 1.5 * iqr
  upper_bound <- q3 + 1.5 * iqr
  return(x < lower_bound | x > upper_bound)
}

# Enhanced function to create narrow boxplots with red outlier detection
create_enhanced_boxplot <- function(data_long, title, subtitle, colors, x_label, y_label, 
                                  variable_col = "variable", value_col = "value", remove_outliers = FALSE) {
  
  # Detect outliers for each variable
  data_with_outliers <- data_long %>%
    group_by(!!sym(variable_col)) %>%
    mutate(
      is_outlier = detect_outliers(!!sym(value_col)),
      outlier_label = ifelse(is_outlier, "Outlier", "Normal")
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  # Remove outliers if requested
  if (remove_outliers) {
    plot_data <- data_with_outliers %>% filter(!is_outlier)
    title <- paste(title, "(Without Outliers)")
  } else {
    plot_data <- data_with_outliers
  }
  
  # Calculate statistics
  stats <- plot_data %>%
    group_by(!!sym(variable_col)) %>%
    summarise(
      median_val = median(!!sym(value_col), na.rm = TRUE),
      iqr_val = IQR(!!sym(value_col), na.rm = TRUE),
      n_obs = sum(!is.na(!!sym(value_col))),
      n_outliers = sum(is_outlier, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = 'drop'
    )
  
  p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes_string(x = variable_col, y = value_col, fill = variable_col)) +
    geom_boxplot(
      alpha = 0.85, 
      outlier.shape = NA,  # Hide default outliers
      width = 0.25,  # Even narrower boxplots
      color = "#000000",  # Clear black contour
      size = 0.8,  # Thicker black border
      show.legend = FALSE
    ) +
    # Add red outlier points manually
    {if (!remove_outliers) {
      geom_point(
        data = plot_data %>% filter(is_outlier),
        aes_string(x = variable_col, y = value_col),
        color = "#DC143C",  # Bright red for outliers
        size = 1.5,
        alpha = 0.8,
        shape = 16,
        inherit.aes = FALSE
      )
    }} +
    stat_summary(
      fun = median, 
      geom = "text", 
      aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", after_stat(y))),
      size = 3.0, 
      color = "white", 
      fontface = "bold",
      vjust = 0.5
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = colors) +
    labs(
      title = title,
      subtitle = subtitle,
      x = x_label,
      y = y_label
    ) +
    publication_theme +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::number_format(accuracy = 0.1)) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off")
  
  return(p)
}

# ENHANCED CORRELATION MATRIX
cat("Creating enhanced correlation matrix...\n")

# Select all numeric variables (keeping ALL variables, even with many NAs)
numeric_vars <- weather_data %>%
  select(-c(date, year, month, day, decade_1, decade, date_2, week, day_of_year, 
            key_0, key_01, key_1, key_2, period)) %>%
  select_if(is.numeric)

# Remove variables that are entirely NA or have insufficient data for correlation
correlation_data <- numeric_vars #%>%
  #select_if(~ sum(!is.na(.)) > 10)  # Keep variables with at least 10 non-NA values

# Calculate correlation matrix with significance testing (using pairwise complete observations)
cor_result <- rcorr(as.matrix(correlation_data), type = "pearson")
cor_matrix <- cor_result$r
p_matrix <- cor_result$P

# Handle any remaining NA/NaN/Inf values in correlation matrix
cor_matrix[is.na(cor_matrix)] <- 0
cor_matrix[is.infinite(cor_matrix)] <- 0

# Create enhanced correlation plot with blue to red palette
png("Enhanced_Weather_Boxplots_Publication/15_Enhanced_Correlation_Matrix.png", 
    width = 20, height = 18, units = "in", res = 300, bg = "white")

# Set up margins for title
par(mar = c(2, 2, 6, 3))

# Use standard blue to red color palette
corr_colors <- colorRampPalette(c("#053061", "#2166AC", "#4393C3", "#92C5DE", 
                                 "#D1E5F0", "#F7F7F7", 
                                 "#FDDBC7", "#F4A582", "#D6604D", "#B2182B", "#67001F"))(100)

# Create the correlation plot with standard blue to red palette
corrplot(cor_matrix,
         method = "color",
         type = "upper",
         order = "original",
         col = corr_colors,
         tl.col = "#000000",
         tl.srt = 45,
         tl.cex = 0.8,
         cl.cex = 1.1,
         title = "Correlation Matrix of Weather Variables\n(Blue to Red Color Palette)",
         mar = c(0,0,4,0),
         diag = FALSE,
         addCoef.col = "#000000",
         number.cex = 0.45,
         number.digits = 2,
         outline = TRUE,
         cl.ratio = 0.2,
         cl.align.text = "c",
         cl.offset = 0.5)

# Add significance stars ABOVE the correlation values (not overlapping)
n_vars <- ncol(cor_matrix)
for(i in 1:(n_vars-1)) {
  for(j in (i+1):n_vars) {
    if(!is.na(p_matrix[i,j])) {
      # Determine significance level
      if(p_matrix[i,j] < 0.001) {
        sig_symbol <- "***"
        sig_color <- "#000000"
        sig_cex <- 0.7
      } else if(p_matrix[i,j] < 0.01) {
        sig_symbol <- "**"
        sig_color <- "#333333"
        sig_cex <- 0.7
      } else if(p_matrix[i,j] < 0.05) {
        sig_symbol <- "*"
        sig_color <- "#666666"
        sig_cex <- 0.7
      } else {
        sig_symbol <- ""
        sig_color <- "black"
        sig_cex <- 0.7
      }
      
      if(sig_symbol != "") {
        # Calculate position ABOVE the correlation value
        x_center <- j
        y_center <- n_vars - i + 1
        
        # Place significance stars ABOVE the correlation coefficient
        text(x_center, y_center + 0.3, sig_symbol, 
             cex = sig_cex, col = sig_color, font = 2)
      }
    }
  }
}

# Enhanced academic legend
legend(x = 10, y = 10,          # 10 units from left and 10 units up from bottom
       legend = c(
         "Statistical Significance:",
         "*** p < 0.001 (highly significant)", 
         "**  p < 0.01 (very significant)", 
         "*   p < 0.05 (significant)",
         "",
         "Correlation Strength:",
         "Red: Strong Positive (r > 0.7)",
         "Light Red: Moderate Positive (0.3 < r ≤ 0.7)", 
         "White: Weak/No Correlation (-0.3 ≤ r ≤ 0.3)",
         "Light Blue: Moderate Negative (-0.7 ≤ r < -0.3)",
         "Blue: Strong Negative (r < -0.7)"
       ), 
       text.col = c("#000000", "#000000", "#333333", "#666666", "white",
                   "#000000", "#B2182B", "#F4A582", "#000000", "#92C5DE", "#2166AC"), 
       bty = "n", 
       cex = 0.85,
       title = "Legend",
       title.col = "#000000",
       title.cex = 1.0)

dev.off()

# CREATE COMPREHENSIVE SUMMARY STATISTICS
cat("Creating comprehensive summary statistics for all variables...\n")

summary_stats <- numeric_vars %>%
  summarise_all(list(
    N = ~sum(!is.na(.)),
    Mean = ~round(mean(., na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    Median = ~round(median(., na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    SD = ~round(sd(., na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    Min = ~round(min(., na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    Max = ~round(max(., na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    Q1 = ~round(quantile(., 0.25, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    Q3 = ~round(quantile(., 0.75, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    Missing = ~sum(is.na(.)),
    Missing_Pct = ~round(sum(is.na(.))/length(.) * 100, 1)
  ), .names = "{.col}__{.fn}") %>%      # <--- use double underscore here
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Variable_Stat", values_to = "Value") %>%
  separate(Variable_Stat, into = c("Variable", "Statistic"), sep = "__") %>%   # <--- split by double underscore
  pivot_wider(names_from = Statistic, values_from = Value) %>%
  arrange(Variable)

# Fix the error in saving summary statistics by converting to data frame first
summary_stats_df <- as.data.frame(summary_stats)

# Save comprehensive summary statistics
write.csv(summary_stats_df, "Enhanced_Weather_Boxplots_Publication/Comprehensive_Summary_Statistics.csv", 
          row.names = FALSE)
```

## III.2. Time Series Analysis

**Description:** Visualize temporal evolution of each weather variable with multiple analytical layers including raw data, rolling averages, trend lines, and outlier identification. Designed to reveal long-term patterns and seasonal cycles.

```{r}
# Function to create individual time series plots
create_individual_timeseries <- function(data, date_col, value_col, 
                                       title, y_label, color,
                                       show_outliers = TRUE, 
                                       show_ci = TRUE,
                                       show_rolling = TRUE,
                                       show_trend = TRUE) {
  
  # Convert date column if not already Date type
  if (!inherits(data[[date_col]], "Date")) {
    data[[date_col]] <- as.Date(data[[date_col]])
  }
  
  # Detect outliers if requested
  if (show_outliers) {
    data$is_outlier <- detect_outliers(data[[value_col]])
  }
  
  # Create base plot
  p <- ggplot(data, aes_string(x = date_col, y = value_col)) +
    publication_theme +
    labs(title = title, y = y_label, x = "Year") +
    scale_x_date(date_labels = "%Y", date_breaks = "1 year") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::number_format(accuracy = 0.1)) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  
  # Add confidence interval if requested (made lighter)
  if (show_ci) {
    p <- p + 
      stat_summary(fun.data = mean_cl_normal, geom = "ribbon", 
                  alpha = 0.1, fill = "#CCCCCC")  # Much lighter CI band
  }
  
  # Add main time series line
  p <- p + 
    geom_line(color = color, size = 0.8, alpha = 0.7)
  
  # Add trend line if requested
  if (show_trend) {
    p <- p + 
      geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, 
                 color = color, linetype = "dashed", size = 1.0, alpha = 0.8)
  }
  
  # Add 30-day rolling mean if requested (more prominent)
  if (show_rolling) {
    roll_data <- data %>%
      mutate(rolling_mean = zoo::rollmean(!!sym(value_col), 30, fill = NA, align = "right"))
    
    p <- p + 
      geom_line(data = roll_data, aes(x = !!sym(date_col), y = rolling_mean),
              color = color, size = 1.4, linetype = "solid", alpha = 0.9)  # More prominent rolling mean
  }
  
  # Add outlier points if requested
  if (show_outliers) {
    p <- p + 
      geom_point(data = data %>% filter(is_outlier),
               aes_string(x = date_col, y = value_col),
               color = "#DC143C", size = 1.5, alpha = 0.8, shape = 16)
  }
  
  return(p)
}

# Get list of all numeric variables (excluding date columns)
numeric_vars <- weather_data %>%
  select(-c(date, year, month, day, decade_1, decade, date_2, week, day_of_year, 
            key_0, key_01, key_1, key_2, period)) %>%
  select_if(is.numeric) %>%
  names()

# Create a plot for each variable
cat("Creating enhanced individual time series plots for each variable...\n")

# Define color assignments for each variable type
var_colors <- c(
  # Temperature
  temp_min = publication_colors$temp_colors[1],
  temp_mean = publication_colors$temp_colors[2],
  temp_max = publication_colors$temp_colors[3],
  temp_amplitude = publication_colors$temp_colors[4],
  temp_senegal = publication_colors$temp_colors[5],
  temp_canal_a = publication_colors$temp_colors[6],
  
  # Humidity
  humidity_min = publication_colors$humidity_colors[1],
  humidity_mean = publication_colors$humidity_colors[2],
  humidity_max = publication_colors$humidity_colors[3],
  humidity_6h = publication_colors$humidity_colors[4],
  humidity_12h = publication_colors$humidity_colors[5],
  humidity_16h = publication_colors$humidity_colors[6],
  humidity_24h = publication_colors$humidity_colors[7],
  
  # Solar
  insolation = publication_colors$solar_colors[1],
  radiation = publication_colors$solar_colors[2],
  
  # Cloud
  cloud_6h = publication_colors$cloud_colors[1],
  cloud_16h = publication_colors$cloud_colors[2],
  
  # Evaporation
```

# IV. Multivariate Data Analysis - PCA

### IV.1. Correlation Analysis

**Description:** Examine linear relationships between all numeric weather variables using Pearson correlation coefficients with significance testing. The correlation matrix reveals multicollinearity and potential predictor relationships.

### IV.2. Principal Component Analysis (PCA)

**Description:** Dimensionality reduction technique to identify the main patterns of variation in the weather data. Transforms correlated variables into uncorrelated principal components that capture maximum variance.

```{r}
# Multivariate Data Analysis using explor package
# Load required libraries
library(explor)
library(FactoMineR)
library(factoextra)
library(corrplot)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)
library(DT)

cat("================================================================\n")
cat("MULTIVARIATE DATA ANALYSIS WITH EXPLOR PACKAGE\n")
cat("================================================================\n")

# Prepare the data for multivariate analysis
cat("Preparing data for multivariate analysis...\n")

# First, let's examine the data structure
cat("Examining weather_data structure...\n")
cat("• Total rows in weather_data:", nrow(weather_data), "\n")
cat("• Total columns:", ncol(weather_data), "\n")
cat("• Column names:", paste(names(weather_data)[1:10], collapse = ", "), "...\n\n")

# Get all numeric variables more carefully
numeric_vars <- weather_data %>%
  select_if(is.numeric) %>%
  select(-any_of(c("year", "month", "day", "decade_1", "decade", "week", "day_of_year", 
                   "key_0", "key_01", "key_1", "key_2", "period"))) %>%
  names()

cat("Identified numeric variables:", length(numeric_vars), "\n")
if(length(numeric_vars) > 0) {
  cat("First 10 variables:", paste(head(numeric_vars, 10), collapse = ", "), "\n")
} else {
  cat("ERROR: No numeric variables found!\n")
  stop("Please check your data structure")
}

# Check for missing values in each variable
missing_summary <- weather_data %>%
  select(all_of(numeric_vars)) %>%
  summarise_all(~sum(is.na(.))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "missing_count") %>%
  mutate(missing_percent = round(missing_count / nrow(weather_data) * 100, 2)) %>%
  arrange(desc(missing_count))

cat("\nMissing values summary (top 10):\n")
print(head(missing_summary, 10))

# Remove variables with too many missing values (>50%)
vars_to_keep <- missing_summary %>%
  filter(missing_percent <= 50) %>%
  pull(variable)

cat("\nKeeping", length(vars_to_keep), "variables with ≤50% missing values\n")

# Create analysis dataset
if("date" %in% names(weather_data)) {
  analysis_data <- weather_data %>%
    select(date, any_of(c("year", "month")), all_of(vars_to_keep))
} else {
  # Create a dummy date if date column doesn't exist
  analysis_data <- weather_data %>%
    mutate(date = seq.Date(from = as.Date("2000-01-01"), 
                          length.out = nrow(weather_data), 
                          by = "day")) %>%
    select(date, any_of(c("year", "month")), all_of(vars_to_keep))
}

# Remove rows with too many missing values (>50% of variables)
analysis_data <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(rowSums(is.na(select(., all_of(vars_to_keep)))) <= length(vars_to_keep) * 0.5)

cat("\nAfter filtering:\n")
cat("• Variables:", length(vars_to_keep), "\n")
cat("• Observations:", nrow(analysis_data), "\n")

if(nrow(analysis_data) > 0) {
  cat("• Date range:", min(analysis_data$date, na.rm = TRUE), "to", max(analysis_data$date, na.rm = TRUE), "\n\n")
} else {
  stop("ERROR: No observations left after filtering!")
}

# Extract numeric data for PCA and handle remaining missing values
pca_data <- analysis_data %>%
  select(all_of(vars_to_keep))

# Replace remaining missing values with column means
pca_data <- pca_data %>%
  mutate_all(~ifelse(is.na(.), mean(., na.rm = TRUE), .))

# Check if we have valid data
if(nrow(pca_data) == 0 || ncol(pca_data) == 0) {
  stop("ERROR: No valid data for PCA analysis!")
}

# Remove variables with zero variance - CORRECTED VERSION
var_check <- apply(pca_data, 2, function(x) {
  if(all(is.na(x))) {
    return(NA)  # Return NA for columns with all missing values
  } else {
    return(var(x, na.rm = TRUE))  # Calculate variance ignoring NAs
  }
})

# Identify problematic columns: zero variance, NA variance, or infinite variance
zero_var_cols <- names(var_check)[var_check == 0 | is.na(var_check) | is.infinite(var_check)]

if(length(zero_var_cols) > 0) {
  cat("Removing", length(zero_var_cols), "variables with zero/NA/infinite variance:\n")
  cat(paste(zero_var_cols, collapse = ", "), "\n\n")
  pca_data <- pca_data %>% select(-all_of(zero_var_cols))
  vars_to_keep <- setdiff(vars_to_keep, zero_var_cols)
} else {
  cat("All variables have valid variance.\n\n")
}

# Scale the data (important for PCA)
pca_data_scaled <- scale(pca_data)

# Add rownames for better identification
rownames(pca_data_scaled) <- paste0("Day_", 1:nrow(pca_data_scaled))

# Update numeric_vars to reflect final variables
numeric_vars <- vars_to_keep

cat("Final dataset for PCA:\n")
cat("• Variables:", ncol(pca_data_scaled), "\n")
cat("• Observations:", nrow(pca_data_scaled), "\n\n")

cat("================================================================\n")
cat("1. PRINCIPAL COMPONENT ANALYSIS (PCA)\n")
cat("================================================================\n")

# Perform PCA using FactoMineR
pca_result <- PCA(pca_data_scaled, 
                  scale.unit = FALSE,  # Already scaled
                  graph = FALSE,       # Don't show default plots
                  ncp = min(10, ncol(pca_data_scaled)))  # Max 10 components

# Launch interactive PCA exploration with explor
cat("Launching interactive PCA exploration...\n")
cat("This will open in your web browser with interactive plots!\n\n")

# Note: This will open an interactive Shiny app
explor(pca_result)

cat("================================================================\n")
cat("2. CORRELATION ANALYSIS\n")
cat("================================================================\n")

# Create correlation matrix
cor_matrix <- cor(pca_data, use = "complete.obs")

# Create output directory if it doesn't exist
if(!dir.exists("Enhanced_Weather_Boxplots_Publication")) {
  dir.create("Enhanced_Weather_Boxplots_Publication", recursive = TRUE)
}

# Plot correlation matrix
png("Enhanced_Weather_Boxplots_Publication/correlation_matrix.png", 
    width = 12, height = 10, units = "in", res = 300)
corrplot(cor_matrix, 
         method = "color",
         type = "upper",
         order = "hclust",
         tl.col = "black",
         tl.srt = 45,
         tl.cex = 0.8,
         col = colorRampPalette(c("#2166AC", "white", "#B2182B"))(100),
         title = "Weather Variables Correlation Matrix",
         mar = c(0,0,2,0))
dev.off()

cat("Correlation matrix saved as correlation_matrix.png\n\n")

cat("================================================================\n")
cat("3. PCA SUMMARY STATISTICS\n")
cat("================================================================\n")

# Print PCA summary
cat("Eigenvalues and variance explained:\n")
print(round(pca_result$eig, 3))

cat("\nVariables with highest contributions to PC1:\n")
contrib_pc1 <- sort(pca_result$var$contrib[,1], decreasing = TRUE)[1:10]
print(round(contrib_pc1, 2))

cat("\nVariables with highest contributions to PC2:\n")
contrib_pc2 <- sort(pca_result$var$contrib[,2], decreasing = TRUE)[1:10]
print(round(contrib_pc2, 2))

cat("\n================================================================\n")
cat("4. ADDITIONAL VISUALIZATIONS\n")
cat("================================================================\n")

# Create scree plot
scree_plot <- fviz_eig(pca_result, addlabels = TRUE, ylim = c(0, 50)) +
  ggtitle("PCA Scree Plot - Variance Explained") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"))

ggsave("Enhanced_Weather_Boxplots_Publication/pca_scree_plot.png", scree_plot,
       width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

# Create biplot
biplot <- fviz_pca_biplot(pca_result, 
                         repel = TRUE,
                         col.var = "#2E9FDF",
                         col.ind = "#696969",
                         alpha.ind = 0.3,
                         title = "PCA Biplot - Variables and Observations") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"))

ggsave("Enhanced_Weather_Boxplots_Publication/pca_biplot.png", biplot,
       width = 12, height = 8, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

# Create variables plot
var_plot <- fviz_pca_var(pca_result,
                        col.var = "contrib",
                        gradient.cols = c("#00AFBB", "#E7B800", "#FC4E07"),
                        repel = TRUE,
                        title = "PCA Variables Plot - Contribution to Components") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"))

ggsave("Enhanced_Weather_Boxplots_Publication/pca_variables_plot.png", var_plot,
       width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

cat("Additional PCA plots saved:\n")
cat("• pca_scree_plot.png - Variance explained by each component\n")
cat("• pca_biplot.png - Variables and observations together\n")
cat("• pca_variables_plot.png - Variables contribution plot\n\n")

cat("================================================================\n")
cat("5. TEMPORAL ANALYSIS WITH PCA SCORES\n")
cat("================================================================\n")

# Extract PCA scores and add date information
pca_scores <- as.data.frame(pca_result$ind$coord)
pca_scores$date <- analysis_data$date
pca_scores$year <- analysis_data$year
pca_scores$month <- analysis_data$month

# Create temporal plots for first 3 PCs
for(i in 1:3) {
  pc_name <- paste0("Dim.", i)
  var_explained <- round(pca_result$eig[i, 2], 1)
  
  temporal_plot <- ggplot(pca_scores, aes_string(x = "date", y = pc_name)) +
    geom_line(color = "#2E9FDF", alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_smooth(method = "loess", color = "#FC4E07", se = TRUE) +
    labs(title = paste0("PC", i, " Time Series (", var_explained, "% variance)"),
         x = "Date", 
         y = paste0("PC", i, " Score")) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12, face = "bold")) +
    scale_x_date(date_labels = "%Y", date_breaks = "1 year") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  
  ggsave(paste0("Enhanced_Weather_Boxplots_Publication/pca_pc", i, "_timeseries.png"), 
         temporal_plot, width = 10, height = 5, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
}

cat("Temporal PCA plots saved:\n")
cat("• pca_pc1_timeseries.png - First principal component over time\n")
cat("• pca_pc2_timeseries.png - Second principal component over time\n")
cat("• pca_pc3_timeseries.png - Third principal component over time\n\n")

cat("================================================================\n")
cat("6. VARIABLE GROUPING ANALYSIS\n")
cat("================================================================\n")

# Group variables by type for better interpretation
var_groups <- list(
  Temperature = grep("temp", numeric_vars, value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE),
  Humidity = grep("humidity", numeric_vars, value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE),
  Solar = grep("insolation|radiation", numeric_vars, value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE),
  Cloud = grep("cloud", numeric_vars, value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE),
  Evaporation = grep("evap", numeric_vars, value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE),
  IGN = grep("ign", numeric_vars, value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)
)

# Print variable groups
cat("Variable groups identified:\n")
for(group_name in names(var_groups)) {
  if(length(var_groups[[group_name]]) > 0) {
    cat("•", group_name, ":", length(var_groups[[group_name]]), "variables\n")
  }
}

# Create a supplementary PCA with group information
cat("\n================================================================\n")
cat("7. SAVE ANALYSIS RESULTS\n")
cat("================================================================\n")

# Save PCA results
save(pca_result, pca_scores, cor_matrix, var_groups, 
     file = "Enhanced_Weather_Boxplots_Publication/multivariate_analysis_results.RData")

# Create summary table
n_components <- min(10, nrow(pca_result$eig))
summary_table <- data.frame(
  Component = paste0("PC", 1:n_components),
  Eigenvalue = round(pca_result$eig[1:n_components, 1], 3),
  Variance_Percent = round(pca_result$eig[1:n_components, 2], 2),
  Cumulative_Percent = round(pca_result$eig[1:n_components, 3], 2)
)

write.csv(summary_table, "Enhanced_Weather_Boxplots_Publication/pca_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

## IV.3. 3x3 PCA Variables Plot

**Description:** Comprehensive visualization showing variable loadings across multiple principal component pairs (PC1-PC2, PC1-PC3, etc.). Each subplot uses consistent sizing, color-coded by contribution or quality (cos²).

```{r}
#3x3 PCA Variables Plot Grid 
# Load required libraries
library(FactoMineR)
library(factoextra)
library(ggplot2)
library(gridExtra)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(viridis)
library(cowplot)

cat("================================================================\n")
cat("CREATING 3x3 PCA VARIABLES PLOT GRID\n")
cat("================================================================\n")

# Define a sophisticated color palette
bold_colors <- c("#FF6B6B", "#4ECDC4", "#45B7D1", "#96CEB4", "#FFEAA7", "#DDA0DD", "#98D8E8", "#F7DC6F", "#BB8FCE")
gradient_colors <- c("#2C3E50", "#E74C3C", "#F39C12", "#F1C40F", "#2ECC71", "#1ABC9C", "#3498DB", "#9B59B6", "#E67E22")

# Create custom theme for bold, professional plots with uniform sizing
theme_pca_bold <- function() {
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    # UNIFORM TEXT SIZING
    plot.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, color = "#2C3E50", margin = margin(b = 8)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, hjust = 0.5, color = "#7F8C8D", margin = margin(b = 6)),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold", color = "#34495E"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 8, color = "#2C3E50"),
    
    # UNIFORM LEGEND STYLING - TALL AND NARROW
    legend.title = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold", color = "#2C3E50", hjust = 0.5),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 7.5, color = "#2C3E50"),
    legend.key.size = unit(0.4, "cm"),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.box = "vertical",
    legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 10),
    legend.box.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
    
    # CONSISTENT GRID AND BACKGROUND
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "#ECF0F1", size = 0.4, linetype = "dashed"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = "#F8F9FA", size = 0.25, linetype = "dotted"),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#FEFEFE", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#FFFFFF", color = NA),
    
    # UNIFORM LEGEND BACKGROUND
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "#F8F9FA", color = "#BDC3C7", size = 0.4),
    legend.key = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA),
    
    # UNIFORM MARGINS FOR CONSISTENCY
    plot.margin = margin(8, 8, 8, 8),
    
    # STRIP TEXT FOR CONSISTENCY
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9, color = "#2C3E50"),
    
    # ENSURE CONSISTENT ASPECT RATIOS
    aspect.ratio = 1
  )
}

# Function to create enhanced PCA variable plot with contours and uniform sizing
create_pca_var_plot <- function(pca_result, axes = c(1, 2), plot_title = "", color_type = "contrib") {
  
  # Get variance explained for axes labels
  var_exp_1 <- round(pca_result$eig[axes[1], 2], 1)
  var_exp_2 <- round(pca_result$eig[axes[2], 2], 1)
  
  # Create base plot
  p <- fviz_pca_var(pca_result,
                    axes = axes,
                    col.var = color_type,
                    alpha.var = 0.8,
                    repel = TRUE,
                    labelsize = 2.8,  # Reduced for uniformity
                    pointsize = 2.0,  # Standardized
                    arrowsize = 0.6,  # Standardized
                    select.var = list(cos2 = 0.3)) # Show only well-represented variables
  
  # Customize the plot with our theme and colors - UNIFORM LEGEND SIZING
  if(color_type == "contrib") {
    p <- p + 
      scale_color_gradient2(low = "#3498DB", mid = "#F39C12", high = "#E74C3C", 
                           midpoint = 50, name = "Contrib\n%",
                           guide = guide_colorbar(title.position = "top", 
                                                title.hjust = 0.5,
                                                barwidth = 1.2,   # Narrower
                                                barheight = 4.5,  # Taller
                                                ticks.colour = "#2C3E50",
                                                ticks.linewidth = 0.5,
                                                frame.colour = "#2C3E50",
                                                frame.linewidth = 0.8)) +
      labs(title = plot_title,
           subtitle = paste0("PC", axes[1], " & PC", axes[2]),
           x = paste0("PC", axes[1], " (", var_exp_1, "%)"),
           y = paste0("PC", axes[2], " (", var_exp_2, "%)"))
  } else if(color_type == "cos2") {
    p <- p + 
      scale_color_viridis_c(option = "plasma", name = "Quality\n(Cos²)",
                           guide = guide_colorbar(title.position = "top", 
                                                title.hjust = 0.5,
                                                barwidth = 1.2,   # Narrower
                                                barheight = 4.5,  # Taller
                                                ticks.colour = "#2C3E50",
                                                ticks.linewidth = 0.5,
                                                frame.colour = "#2C3E50",
                                                frame.linewidth = 0.8)) +
      labs(title = plot_title,
           subtitle = paste0("PC", axes[1], " & PC", axes[2]),
           x = paste0("PC", axes[1], " (", var_exp_1, "%)"),
           y = paste0("PC", axes[2], " (", var_exp_2, "%)"))
  } else {
    p <- p + 
      scale_color_manual(values = bold_colors, name = "Variable\nGroups") +
      labs(title = plot_title,
           subtitle = paste0("PC", axes[1], " & PC", axes[2]),
           x = paste0("PC", axes[1], " (", var_exp_1, "%)"),
           y = paste0("PC", axes[2], " (", var_exp_2, "%)"))
  }
  
  # Apply custom theme
  p <- p + theme_pca_bold()
  
  # Add contour-like effect with confidence ellipse and grid enhancement
  p <- p + 
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", color = "#7F8C8D", size = 0.8, alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", color = "#7F8C8D", size = 0.8, alpha = 0.7) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, 
             fill = NA, color = "#2C3E50", size = 1.2) +
    # ENSURE UNIFORM PLOT AREA AND AXIS LIMITS
    coord_fixed(ratio = 1, 
               xlim = c(-1.1, 1.1), 
               ylim = c(-1.1, 1.1),
               expand = FALSE, 
               clip = "on")
  
  return(p)
}

# Define the 9 different dimension combinations for the 3x3 grid
plot_combinations <- list(
```
